D41·48ck — 2026-10-11
chose: 3.9 gate rule, fixed before any native rep was scored: project every rework case of the 2.5 and 3.4 agent reps (a handoff that left its task undone, then the next session on that task) call by call from both transcripts, at two bounds. LOWER, the thread's best case: it skips the retry's calls before its first edit and resumes on the 3.3 packet alone (400 tokens). UPPER: it replays every retry call on its larger base and resumes with the retry's own session-start tail. Price at the weights the adapter's reported cost fits (fresh input 1, one-hour cache write 2, cache read 0.1, output 5, at $2/M; within 0.3% on all 21 reps), with the one-hour TTL the transcripts show. A lever (warm resume, cold resume, checkpoint fork) goes ahead for a kind of case only if, at both bounds, it is below both fresh sessions (plain and 3.3-packet) on raw tokens and on price, and every arm holding such cases, run that way at the lower bound, is below the native arm per task on both.
over: A single point estimate; raw tokens alone or price alone; judging against fresh sessions without the native arm
because: The operator builds threads only once they are proven efficient (2026-10-11), and a lever that wins only in its best case is not proven. Raw tokens count a cache read as a fresh token, while price alone hides the token count the operator named, so the rule holds both. A lever that beats fresh sessions but leaves sofar above native workflows does not do what the operator asked.
